open_questions: Depth scatter across sectors (3446 to 1802 ppm, depth_change_pct 62.04, sectors.p_constant 0.06054) but p_constant not significant; follow-up photometry can test stability
Star is spotted (rotation amplitude 15530-24556 ppm, period 5.199 d) with RV not measured yet; mass measurement could confirm density
dossier.public_summary: TESS shows a short, flat-bottomed 0.28% dip every 1.38 days on an M dwarf, consistent with a 2.6 Earth-radius planet. Centroiding puts the signal on the target and rules out nearby stars that could mimic it, with no odd-even or secondary eclipse to indicate a binary.

reasons.why: Planet-sized below 10 Rearth (2.55 Rearth from TIC, 2.85 Rearth from Gaia FLAME/GSP-Phot) favours a planet over a small-star eclipse.
Strong negative V-shape statistic indicates flat-bottomed transit, favours planet over grazing binary.

Difference imaging places dip on target (offset 3.727 arcsec, 1.98 sigma); closest star that could cause is 8.2 sigma away, ruling out plausible neighbour with 11.7 arcsec, 1.54 delta_mag, eclipse_needed 0.0115.
No odd/even difference (2611 vs 2555 ppm) argues against binary at twice the 1.38-d period.
No significant secondary (SNR 2.589 <5, below best_brightening_snr 2.142) argues against close eclipsing binary on target.
Observed duration 0.9927 h vs central 1.159 h gives ratio 0.86 (0.77 with Gaia FLAME radius 0.481), consistent with a central transit, not mis-fit.
High-SNR signal seen in 58 transits with share 0.09242 not dominated by few events, not a noise spike.
